facts.value: With valid EventPriority payloads, ret->next overlays the FIRST word because HSD_SList.next is its first field. The comparison therefore detects an already registered event, returns that payload cast as HSD_SList*, and leaves its priority unchanged. Otherwise the full scan remembers the last node with priority <= requested priority and allocates a new payload at end. Append after a nonnull anchor returns the anchor, not the new node; prepend updates the global head and returns the new head. Allocation has no local payload-null guard.

facts.value: Callback records flow from the global registry into callback invocation, and each returned linked item enters one of three rendering paths. Text is scanned for visible width while excluding supported backslash controls, then passed with a default color and computed cell origin to the formatted-text renderer. Gradient data is drawn across a 600-unit line. Positive bar counts are first summed and then converted with their colors into proportional horizontal segments for the ticked-line renderer. Shared row and column accumulators carry layout state across callbacks and item chains.

facts.value: Starts at column 60, line 1.0, first-item flag set. Text exceeding column 60 wraps by a full line, then advances by counted width plus two. Gradient and nonempty positive-bar sequences move by half a line when the column is nonzero and leave column 60. Empty registry, null item chains and nonpositive bar totals draw no items; unknown item types are skipped. Background alpha initializes to zero. Each text item starts white; color controls mutate only its local color. There is no callback-null, malformed-string, bar/gradient-bound or registry-mutation guard, and no item freeing.
